data.reason: Modem re-registered and is OPERATIONAL since ~02:28 (modem-events.jsonl: "registration complete"), but gw.lan still holds its pre-reboot WAN address 198.51.100.27 and cannot reach the gateway 198.51.100.1 (100% loss). The WAN watchdog only logged would_reload events in observe mode, so the WAN DHCP lease was never renewed. Reconfiguring the WAN interface should reacquire a lease from the modem and restore internet.

data.cause: The WAN DHCP lease on gw.lan became stale when the cable modem dropped its link (~02:01, T3 timeout), lost its config file (TFTP NOT FOUND) and rebooted into a new registration by 02:28; the firewall still holds the old address 198.51.100.27 and cannot reach the ISP gateway, so traffic is not getting through even though the modem is now operational.
evidence: ip route shows default via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 with local address 198.51.100.27 while 'ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1' gets 100% packet loss — the gateway learned from the pre-reboot modem is no longer answering

modem-events.jsonl: 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out', 02:14:10 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND', 02:28:21 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' — matches the outage start ~02:01 and shows the modem recovered before now
modem-metrics.jsonl at 02:40: cm_status OPERATIONAL, min_snr 37.9 dB, modem uptime 2280s (boots ~02:02) — the provider side is up, so the fault is not an ongoing line problem

state.json: reloads_in_outage 2, last_action reload, but events.jsonl shows only 'would_reload' entries because the watchdog runs in observe mode — the WAN was never actually reconfigured after the modem came back
ifconfig vtnet0: UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP, active — the physical WAN link on the firewall itself is fine
data.recommendation: Renew the WAN DHCP lease on gw.lan (wan_reload, already requested; preconditions met). The modem itself also had a config-file/TFTP failure before it recovered, so if outages recur with the same TFTP message, raise it with the ISP. Longer term, consider moving the WAN watchdog from observe mode to enforcing so a stale lease is auto-renewed once the modem reports OPERATIONAL and has settled.
